title: Dedicated throughput SLO PRD + tier proposal (Standard/Performance/Premium)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
Goal
Produce a publish-ready PRD and tier proposal for Redwood Dedicated throughput guarantees, aligned across Product, Runtime, Infra, SRE, Finance/Legal, and GTM.

This ticket is the “source of truth” issue for the spec pack and signoff process.

Context / problem
Dedicated customers are buying predictability, but today:
- sales proposals reference inconsistent metrics (req/sec vs tokens/sec; peak vs sustained; p50 vs p95)
- SRE cannot reliably alert/enforce because objectives are not measurable in a standard way
- runtime behavior (batching/scheduling/backpressure) and fleet constraints (shape availability, MIG/no-MIG) are not encoded into the tier promise

We need: one definition of throughput, clear tier semantics (including burst/overload behavior), and a mapping from tier -> shapes -> operational policies -> contract language.

Primary deliverables (Confluence)
1) PRD (Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions)
   - Path: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-throughput-slo-prd.json
   - Contents: customer problem, goals/non-goals, tier matrix v1, success metrics, rollout plan, open questions

2) Throughput measurement standard (company-wide reference)
   - Path: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/throughput-measurement-standard.json
   - Contents: metric definitions, sampling window, normalization rules, exclusions

3) ADRs
   - Primary metric ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0127-dedicated-throughput-primary-metric.json
   - Tier semantics + burst policy ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0128-tiering-model-and-burst-policy.json

4) Published tier definitions (Packaging page)
   - Path: sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-tier-definitions.json
   - Contents: tier feature table, supported shapes, regional constraints, objectives, burst + overload behavior, reporting

- Tier matrix v1 sheet: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/dedicated/tier-matrix-v1-sheet.json

Stakeholders / signoff required

- Finance & Legal: Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra / Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes
- GTM: Jordan Blake / Stephanie Nguyen (sales enablement)
- CS/Support readiness: Jasmine Liu / Owen Phillips

Scope
In-scope for this spec pack:
- Formal definition of “throughput” for Dedicated: primary metric, measurement window, exclusions
- Tier definitions: Standard / Performance / Premium
  - minimum sustained throughput objective and how it is stated (including assumptions)
  - concurrency assumptions and tail-latency guardrails
  - burst allowance and overload behavior (throttle vs shed; what counts as breach vs expected throttling)
- Mapping tiers to supported hardware shapes (single-node vs multi-node; MIG/no-MIG; NVLink constraints)
- Observability + reporting requirements: dashboards, exportable customer-visible metrics, internal alerting
- Enforcement approach: admission control/backpressure behavior; what happens when SLO is at risk
- Packaging guidance: what Sales can promise; exceptions process; pointers to contract language

Out of scope (explicit)
- Rewriting Dedicated provisioning pipeline
- Per-customer bespoke kernel tuning (separate perf engagement)
- Full Console redesign (only minimal surface area to show tier + throughput status)

Proposed tier semantics (draft for review; final values live in tier matrix sheet)
- Standard: “predictable baseline” for general prod workloads; conservative burst; broad regional availability
- Performance: higher sustained throughput + tighter tail latency guardrails; controlled burst; more limited region/shape set
- Premium: highest sustained throughput; prioritized capacity options; strict region/shape constraints; strongest reporting and operational guarantees

Key decisions needed (must be resolved before publish)
1) Primary metric to guarantee (tokens/sec vs req/sec; output-only vs input+output; aggregate method)
2) Windowing/aggregation (e.g., per-deployment sustained rate over N-minute window; treatment of partial outages)
3) Exclusions/carve-outs (maintenance windows, customer-induced errors, invalid requests, model changes, non-compliant context distributions)
4) Burst semantics and overload mode (how we throttle; how we message “expected throttling” vs “SLO breach”)
5) Shape mapping + availability constraints (and how we communicate supply volatility per region)
6) Remedies/credits coupling (how measurement standard is referenced; what triggers credits)

Success metrics
- Internal alignment: single tier promise used by Sales, SRE, Runtime, and contract templates
- Pilot readiness: at least 2 design partners can be quoted using the new tiers without bespoke language
- Operational readiness: dashboards and alerting spec is sufficient for SRE to implement (no “undefined metric” gaps)

Acceptance criteria
Publish-ready (meets “Done” definition) when:
1) PRD is complete and reviewed by Runtime + SRE + Infra (commented and resolved)
2) Measurement standard is finalized and referenced by:
   - ADR-0127 (primary metric)
   - Dedicated throughput SLO definition doc (SRE)
   - contract language draft (Legal)
3) Tier definitions page includes:
   - tier table (Standard/Performance/Premium)
   - objective statement per tier (with measurement window + assumptions)
   - burst/overload behavior description
   - supported shapes + explicit regional constraints
   - customer-visible reporting commitments
4) Open questions log is updated with:
   - final decisions + links to ADRs
   - remaining follow-ups clearly assigned (owner + due date)
5) Stakeholder signoff recorded (explicit “approved” from Product DRI + Runtime + SRE + Infra; Legal + Finance “approved with notes” acceptable if notes are tracked to PM-491/PM-487)
6) Links added in this ticket to final Confluence pages and the tier matrix v1 sheet

Execution plan (this ticket)
- Week 1–2: discovery + baselining assumptions; align on measurement and exclusions
- Week 2–4: draft PRD + ADRs + tier matrix; iterate with SRE/Infra/Runtime
- Week 4+: handoff to implementation epics (metrics, dashboards, admission control) + GTM enablement

Notes for reviewers
- Please review with two hats:
  1) “Can SRE measure/alert this?” (must be computable from emitted metrics)
  2) “Can Sales explain this to a buyer without a 30-minute caveat list?” (must be simple + defensible)
comments: 2025-01-14 (Lauren Bishop): Creating umbrella issue for PRD + tier proposal. Please keep all decision links (ADR + Confluence) attached here so Sales/Legal stop chasing scattered docs.

2025-01-16 (Talia Benson): Draft PRD outline created; added sections for (a) measurement standard references and (b) tier semantics including overload/throttling behaviors. Next: schedule 45 min with SRE to align on windowing + alert semantics.

2025-01-18 (Irene Choi): FYI shape availability varies significantly by region for H100 right now. We should treat Premium as region-limited at launch (and write that into the tier definitions page explicitly). Also, prefer no-MIG for Premium; MIG is ok for Standard depending on model size.

2025-01-22 (Aisha Bello): From SRE perspective, we need a single SLI that maps to both alerting and credits. Suggest sustained output tokens/sec over a rolling window. Please include explicit exclusions: planned maintenance, customer-requested model changes, invalid requests, and customer-driven overload beyond tier burst policy (in which case throttling is expected, not a breach).

2025-01-24 (Sofia Ivanova): Runtime note: if we define throughput as output tokens/sec, we must clarify how we treat streaming. We can measure emitted tokens at the gateway, but decoding stalls during client backpressure will look like throughput drops. Recommend including a carve-out for client-side slow-read / network backpressure or measure at server emission boundary only.

2025-01-28 (Jordan Blake): Sales needs a simple statement we can put in proposals: 'minimum sustained throughput under stated workload assumptions' + what we do when customer exceeds it (throttling vs scale). Please avoid anything that sounds like we guarantee latency at all times during burst; instead define burst as 'best-effort up to X for Y minutes' with explicit throttling behavior.

2025-02-03 (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed draft PRD: good structure. Biggest gap is tying tier objective to an actual dashboard panel + alert. Please ensure the PRD references the dashboards spec and names the metric labels required (deployment_id, tier, model, region).

2025-02-07 (Lauren Bishop): Sent 'final feedback' email to SRE/Infra/Runtime. Requesting explicit approvals by EOD 2/10 so we can publish Confluence pages and unblock PM-491 (contract language). Outstanding: settle burst semantics wording and confirm Standard/Performance availability regions.
